exposure: iron deficiency (P-ferritin <15 ug/L) in the second trimester (24-28 weeks gestation)
cohort: Singleton pregnant women at a single center in Denmark, with blood samples drawn between 24 and 28 weeks gestation.
finding: Second trimester iron deficiency was frequent among pregnant Danish women and associated with accelerated placental and infant growth (higher placental weight, birth weight, birth weight z-score, and lower prevalence of SGA), but not with adverse maternal or infant outcomes.
mod_finding: Second trimester iron deficiency was not associated with emergency cesarean section or induction of labor.
